data.text:
## app-shell — App shell (pattern, archetype navigate)
The persistent frame around an application’s content: global navigation, identity, search, and the region where content changes.
Aliases: application frame, chrome, navigation shell, scaffold
Anatomy: Global navigation (Top-level destinations); Top bar (Title, search and account); Content region (Where destinations render); Secondary navigation (Destinations within a destination)
Related — uses: tabs, drawer, menu, badge, breadcrumbs, tree-view | specializes: navigate | neighbors: split-pane, command-palette
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Navigation placement [layout] — Where are primary and secondary navigation?
  - primary (single-select: one id) — Primary navigation
      top-navigation-bar: Top navigation bar (e.g. GitHub)
      sidebar: Sidebar (e.g. Notion)
      navigation-rail: Navigation rail (e.g. Material 3 rail on tablets)
      bottom-tab-bar: Bottom tab bar (e.g. Instagram)
      drawer: Drawer (e.g. Gmail on Android)
      tab-bar-that-expands-to-sidebar: Tab bar that expands to sidebar (e.g. iPadOS 18 tab bar)
  - secondary (single-select: one id) — Secondary navigation
      none: None (e.g. Instagram)
      second-sidebar-column: Second sidebar column (e.g. Discord channel list beside the server rail)
      sub-tabs-under-the-header: Sub-tabs under the header (e.g. GitHub repository tabs)
      contextual-panel: Contextual panel (e.g. Settings sub-pages)
* Navigation items [content] — What does navigation contain, and how does it change?
  - items (multi-select: list of ids) — Items
      fixed-destinations: Fixed destinations (e.g. Instagram tabs)
      user-pinned-items: User-pinned items (e.g. Notion favourites)
      recents: Recents (e.g. Figma recents)
      live-counts: Live counts — Unread or pending badges (e.g. Slack unreads)
      workspace-switcher: Workspace switcher (e.g. Discord server rail)
* Show and hide [invocation] — Is the shell always there?
  - visibility (single-select: one id) — Visibility
      always-visible: Always visible (e.g. Slack)
      toggle-button: Toggle button (e.g. Gmail collapse menu)
      collapse-on-scroll: Collapse on scroll (e.g. Safari on iOS toolbar)
      reveal-on-hover: Reveal on hover (e.g. Edge vertical tabs collapsed)
* Responsive shell [adaptation] — What happens as the screen narrows?
  - narrowing (single-select: one id) — Narrowing
      collapse-to-icons: Collapse to icons (e.g. Gmail icon rail)
      become-bottom-tabs: Become bottom tabs (e.g. Cross-platform apps)
      become-drawer: Become drawer (e.g. Material responsive layouts)
      hide-in-immersive-mode: Hide in immersive mode (e.g. Full-screen reading and video)
* Workspace structure [composition] — How many applications or workspaces does one shell hold?
  - structure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      single-app: Single app (e.g. Most apps)
      multi-workspace-rail: Multi-workspace rail (e.g. Discord servers)
      mini-apps-inside-an-app: Mini-apps inside an app (e.g. WeChat Mini Programs)
      document-tabs: Document tabs (e.g. Browsers, Figma file tabs)

## file-manager — File manager (pattern, archetype browse-collections)
Browse, organize, preview and act on files and folders arranged in a hierarchy of locations.
Aliases: file browser, Finder, Explorer, drive
Anatomy: Locations (Sidebar of places and favourites); Path (Where you are); Item area (Files and folders here); Preview (A look at the selected file); Toolbar (View and file operations)
Related — uses: tree-view, breadcrumbs, split-pane, tabs, menu, drag-reorder | specializes: overview-detail | neighbors: data-table
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Item view [layout] — How are files shown, and where does a preview appear?
  - view (single-select: one id) — Item view
      icons: Icons (e.g. Finder icon view)
      list: List (e.g. Finder list view)
      columns: Columns — Miller columns, one per level

data.text:
## chart — Chart (pattern, archetype analyze)
A visual encoding of data values as marks and channels so a person can see distributions, comparisons and trends.
Aliases: plot, graph, visualization
Anatomy: Marks (The visual elements); Axes and scales (How values map to space); Legend (How channels are decoded); Tooltip (Detail on demand for a mark); Controls (Encoding and filter affordances)
Related — uses: tooltip, filter-controls, stat-tile | specializes: analyze | neighbors: coordinated-views, pivot-table, dashboard
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Mark encoding [encoding] — What marks and channels carry the data?
  - markType (single-select: one id) — Mark type
      points: Points (e.g. Scatterplots)
      bars: Bars (e.g. Bar charts)
      lines: Lines (e.g. Line charts)
      areas: Areas (e.g. Area charts)
      arcs: Arcs (e.g. Pie and donut)
      cells: Cells (e.g. Heatmaps)
      glyphs: Glyphs (e.g. Radar and parallel coordinates)
  - channels (multi-select: list of ids) — Channels used
      position: Position (e.g. Cartesian plots)
      length: Length (e.g. Bars)
      colour-hue-or-value: Colour hue or value (e.g. Choropleths)
      size: Size (e.g. Bubble charts)
      shape: Shape (e.g. Categorical scatters)
      opacity: Opacity (e.g. Overplotting control)
      animation: Animation — A variable — almost always time — is mapped to motion over frames rather than to a static visual channel, with a play control and a scrubber; bar chart races, animated scatter trails (e.g. Flourish — Bar chart race)
* Scale and axes [layout] — How is the value space laid out?
  - scale (single-select: one id) — Scale
      linear: Linear (e.g. Most charts)
      logarithmic: Logarithmic (e.g. Finance log scales)
      ordinal-or-band: Ordinal or band (e.g. Category axes)
      time: Time (e.g. Time-series axes)
      radial: Radial (e.g. Polar charts)
  - faceting (single-select: one id) — Facet or small multiples
      single-plot: Single plot (e.g. Simple charts)
      small-multiples: Small multiples (e.g. Tableau trellis)
      layered-series: Layered series (e.g. Multi-series lines)
      dual-axis: Dual axis (e.g. Combo charts)
* Mark interrogation [invocation] — How does a person inspect a mark?
  - inspectBy (multi-select: list of ids) — Inspect by
      hover-tooltip: Hover tooltip (e.g. Observable Plot)
      click-to-select: Click to select (e.g. Tableau marks)
      brush-a-region: Brush a region (e.g. D3 brushing)
      cross-filter-linked-views: Cross-filter linked views (e.g. Power BI cross-highlight)
      click-through-to-source-rows: Click-through to source rows (e.g. Tableau View Data)
* Encoding authorship [initiative] — Who chooses the encoding?
  - authorship (single-select: one id) — Authorship
      author-specified: Author-specified (e.g. News graphics)
      builder-ui: Builder UI (e.g. Tableau shelves)
      recommended-chart-type: Recommended chart type (e.g. Excel Recommended Charts)
      generated-from-a-question: Generated from a question (e.g. Tableau Ask Data)
* Annotation and emphasis [feedback] — How are findings called out on the chart?
  - annotation (multi-select: list of ids) — Annotation
      none: None (e.g. Raw plots)
      reference-lines: Reference lines (e.g. Tableau analytics pane)
      callout-labels: Callout labels (e.g. Datawrapper)
      story-points: Story points (e.g. Tableau Stories)
      automated-insight-captions: Automated insight captions (e.g. Power BI smart narratives)
* Responsive encoding [adaptation] — How does the chart change with space and density?
  - adaptation (single-select: one id) — Adaptation
      fixed-desktop-chart: Fixed desktop chart (e.g. Classic BI)
      reflow-for-narrow-screens: Reflow for narrow screens (e.g. Responsive Observable notebooks)
      aggregate-when-dense: Aggregate when dense (e.g. Hexbin overplotting)
      switch-mark-type-by-size: Switch mark type by size (e.g. Mobile chart simplification)

## autocomplete — Autocomplete (component, archetype enter-data)
Suggestions that appear as a person types, completing or replacing the input.
Aliases: typeahead, combobox, suggestions
Anatomy: Input (Where typing happens); Suggestion list (What is proposed); Highlight (The current suggestion)
Related — neighbors: text-field, inline-suggestion, command-palette
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Suggestion types [content] — What is suggested?
  - types (multi-select: list of ids) — Types
      query-completions: Query completions (e.g. Google)
      entities-with-images: Entities with images (e.g. Spotify search)
      recent-inputs: Recent inputs (e.g. Recent searches)
      commands: Commands (e.g. Command palettes)
      people: People (e.g. Email recipient fields)
      text-continuation: Text continuation — The suggestion continues the prose or code being written (next words, a sentence, a code block) rather than completing a query or naming an entity (e.g. Gmail — Smart Compose in the body)
      places-and-addresses: Places and addresses — Street addresses, cities, regions or venues from a geocoder or place index — the codebook's own 'address' frame has no type for them (e.g. Google Maps — Search here)
      records-or-entities: Records or entities — Objects from a known set — addresses, places, records — listed as plain rows with no artwork; the existing entity variation requires images (e.g. Google Maps — Search here)
      code-symbols: Code symbols — Identifiers, methods and keywords from the code's symbol table, each carrying a type icon and documentation. (e.g. VS Code — IntelliSense)
      symbols-in-scope: Symbols in scope — Identifiers, methods and properties that are legal at the cursor, offered with their type and documentation (e.g. VS Code — IntelliSense)
* Source [initiative] — Where do suggestions come from?
  - source (single-select: one id) — Source
      prefix-match: Prefix match (e.g. Country selectors)
      popular-queries: Popular queries (e.g. Search engines)
      personal-history: Personal history (e.g. Browser address bars)
      model-prediction: Model prediction (e.g. Gmail Smart Compose)
* Presentation [layout] — How are suggestions shown?
  - presentation (single-select: one id) — Presentation
      dropdown-list: Dropdown list (e.g. Most comboboxes)
      ghost-text-inline: Ghost text inline (e.g. Smart Compose, fish shell)
      grouped-sections: Grouped sections (e.g. Spotlight)
      full-screen-on-mobile: Full screen on mobile (e.g. Mobile search)
      suggestion-bar: Suggestion bar — A horizontal strip of a few candidates above a keyboard or input, not a list and not inline (iOS QuickType) (e.g. iOS keyboard — QuickType bar)
* Acceptance [invocation] — How is a suggestion taken?
  - accept (multi-select: list of ids) — Accept by
      click: Click (e.g. All)
      enter: Enter (e.g. Search boxes)
      tab: Tab (e.g. Ghost text)
      arrow-keys: Arrow keys (e.g. WAI-ARIA combobox)
* Freedom [scope] — Must the value come from the suggestions?
  - freedom (single-select: one id) — Freedom
      must-choose: Must choose (e.g. Strict comboboxes)
      free-text-allowed: Free text allowed (e.g. Search)
      creates-new-values: Creates new values (e.g. Tag inputs)

## command-palette — Command palette (pattern, archetype navigate)
A keyboard-summoned search box that finds and runs commands, jumps to places and objects, and teaches shortcuts along the way.
Aliases: command bar, quick open, launcher, Cmd+K menu
Anatomy: Trigger (The shortcut or button that summons it); Query (The typed text); Results (Ranked commands, places and objects); Arguments (Follow-up inputs a command needs)
Related — uses: autocomplete, modal-dialog, menu | specializes: navigate | neighbors: search-results, menu
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Results [content] — What can be found, and what does each result show?
  - types (multi-select: list of ids) — R
